description: BusMezzo is a dynamic transit simulation model built on the Mezzo mesoscopic traffic simulator, designed to evaluate operations planning and real-time control of large public transport systems. Oded Cats, Wilco Burghout, Tomer Toledo and Haris Koutsopoulos of KTH Royal Institute of Technology and Technion described it in Transportation Research Record in 2010. Unlike most earlier transit simulators it runs on a mesoscopic traffic platform, which allows large networks while representing the main sources of service uncertainty and stochasticity: traffic conditions, passenger demand and dwell times, and vehicle operations. Applied to a high-demand bus line in metropolitan Tel Aviv under several scenarios, it reproduced bus bunching realistically, and simulated running times and headway distributions matched field data. Coverage: generic; demonstrated on Tel Aviv. Access: the paper is behind the publisher paywall, and a public code release was not confirmed on a provider page during this pass. Licence and cost: paper under publisher copyright; software terms on request from the authors. Caveats: the 2010 description covers a single bus line application, and model details beyond the paper were not checked. It supports network flow, agent-based and capacity planning studies of bus and transit operations. It relates to SUMO, MATSim and the buskit bunching toolkit in the catalogue.
